title: I took a night job watching an empty parking garage. Rule four says never count the cars.
story:
The listing said overnight security, no experience needed, twenty-two dollars an hour. The manager handed me a laminated card with four rules on it and left before I finished reading.

Rule one. Walk the ramps at midnight and at three.

Rule two. If the elevator opens on its own, do not get in.

Rule three. Keep the booth radio on the static station.

Rule four. Never count the cars.

I made it two weeks. Then one slow night, bored out of my mind, I counted them anyway. Level three had nineteen cars. I wrote the number down.

At three, I walked the ramps again. Level three had twenty.

The new one was parked in the corner space, nose out, engine ticking like it had just been driven. A gray sedan, exactly like mine. Same dent in the bumper. Same parking pass in the window.

I ran back to the booth and pulled up the camera for level one, where I always park.

My car was still there. Someone was sitting in the driver's seat.

They turned toward the camera and waved.

The radio wasn't playing static anymore.

It was playing my breathing.
premise: Night guard breaks 'never count the cars' rule; a duplicate of his car appears; someone sits in his real car; radio plays his breathing.
